question: Of the patients with an normal level of IGG, how many of them admitted to the hospital?
evidence: normal level of IGG refers to 900 < IGG < 2000; admitted to the hospital refers to Admission = '+';
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.IGG > 900 AND T2.IGG < 2000 AND T1.Admission = '+'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.IGG > 900 AND T2.IGG <2000 AND  T1.Admission = '+'

d.request: How many distinct patient IDs have an IGG level between 900 and 2000 and an Admission value of '+'?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.IGG BETWEEN 900 AND 2000 AND p.Admission = '+';

b.request: How many distinct patients have at least one laboratory IGG result greater than 900 and less than 2000 and have Admission = '+'?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.IGG > 900 AND l.IGG < 2000 AND p.Admission = '+';

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.IGG > 900 AND l.IGG < 2000 AND p.Admission = '+';
